conflicts.description: Slab pour (A-2003, 8 h) and epoxy coating (A-2009, 6 h) both want the 05:00-10:00 compliant band on the FAB2 L3 deck — 5 open hours, 12 demanded.
Slipping the coating (A-2009) to the next clean window would push the near-critical deck weld (A-2006) and consume four days of its float.

steps.title: Scanned 328 activities in the 72 h lookahead
steps.detail: Listed every activity whose planned window falls inside the rolling 72 h horizon for site NPX-FAB-P2.

steps.title: Flagged 41 of 328 as at-risk
steps.detail: Ran the deterministic window engine on each activity (thermal twin -> evaluate_window). 41 are at_risk, non_compliant or insufficient_window.

steps.title: 2 conflicts on the FAB2 L3 deck
steps.detail: Grouped the flagged activities by work face and shift; two sets compete for the same compliant hours on WF-FAB2-11.

steps.title: Propose: split the coating around the pour
steps.detail: The pour cannot move (hold point: city inspector). Split the 6 h coating into 2 h before the pour crew arrives and 4 h after the deck clears, both inside the dew-point-compliant band.

tool_calls.result_summary: feasible: 2 h + 4 h, 0.5 d float consumed

proposal.rationale: The pour holds a city-inspector hold point and cannot move, but the coating can run in two passes without breaching recoat limits. Splitting keeps both inside the 05:00-10:00 window and spends only half a day of float.

steps.title: Gate: approve the split
steps.detail: Policy engine approved — float consumed is under the near-critical cap.

gate.reason: Split keeps both activities inside their compliant windows and consumes 0.5 d of float, under the 3.0 d cap for a near-critical activity.

steps.title: Split A-2009 into two passes
steps.detail: Applied the approved split via the gated tool.

tool_calls.result_summary: A-2009 split into A-2009a (2 h) + A-2009b (4 h)

steps.title: Verify: both activities now compliant
steps.detail: Re-evaluated A-2003 and both coating segments against the new plan — all sit inside compliant windows.

steps.title: Propose: slip the coating to the next clean window
steps.detail: The cheapest fix for C2 is to shift the coating a day to the next dew-point-compliant window. The solver reports it would push near-critical A-2006 and consume four days of its float.

tool_calls.result_summary: feasible but 4.0 d float consumed on near-critical A-2006

proposal.rationale: A one-day slip clears the dew-point conflict cleanly, but it cascades onto the near-critical deck weld and burns four days of float — more than policy allows an unattended agent to spend. Flagging the tradeoff rather than taking it.

steps.title: Gate: deny — over the float cap
steps.detail: Policy rule max_float_days_consumed caps float consumption at 3.0 d for a near-critical activity; this proposal spends 4.0 d. Denied and routed to a human.

gate.reason: Denied: the shift would spend 4.0 d of float on near-critical A-2006, over the 3.0 d cap. No compliant sequence preserves the milestone — escalating to the superintendent with the tradeoff.

steps.title: Escalate to the superintendent
steps.detail: No compliant sequence preserves the milestone without spending more float than policy permits. Options handed up: (1) accept the 4 d float hit, (2) authorise a dehumidified enclosure to coat in place, (3) an RFI to relax the recoat window. Rule cited: max_float_days_consumed.

tool_calls.result_summary: escalation drafted with three costed options and the rule cited

steps.title: Appended the run to the record
steps.detail: Two record entries written to the hash chain: the approved split and the escalation. A claims consultant can re-derive both from the FortyGuard handles.
